title: Meta AI Open-Sources Rebalancer: A C++ Assignment Solver That Runs About 40 Million Placement Problems a Day
source_used: Engineering at Meta (original blog, read instead of blocked MarkTechPost)
key_facts: Meta open-sourced Rebalancer, a library it says has solved resource-allocation problems across its systems for over nine years.
It solves 'assignment problems': placing objects such as tasks, servers or racks into bins such as servers or data centres under constraints.
Meta says it is used for roughly 40 million assignment problems a day with more than 30 problem formulations.
The P99 solve time is 12 seconds on a problem with 265,000 objects and 3,200 bins.
It offers an optimal solver (using solvers such as Gurobi or HiGHS) and a faster local-search solver; Meta says almost all large problems use local search.
The Meta blog post is dated 21 Sep 2026; MarkTechPost covered it on 6 Oct 2026.
quote_evidence: At the time of this writing, Rebalancer is used to solve roughly 40 million assignment problems every day with more than 30 unique problem formulations.
We’re open-sourcing Rebalancer, the assignment-problem solver that has been used to solve resource allocation problems throughout Meta for over nine years.
why_it_matters_hint: Other companies can reuse the tool Meta uses to decide where workloads and hardware go.
